_doc: S03 seed semester. Dates are relative to load time (see backend/app/db/seed_dates.py). Refs: 'course/material#n' (n = page, or transcript window number) and 'course/post:key'. IDs are uuid5('hackumass-mock/<kind>/<key>') to match backend/app/api/mock_data.py.

changes.old: HW 5 on dynamic programming is posted. Start early: problems 3 and 4 (LCS and edit distance) take longer than they look. For every problem I want the recurrence written in words first, then the table, then the running time.

cards.back: Solutions to subproblems, so each one is computed only once.
O(nW): pseudo-polynomial, because W is a number, not an input length.

cards.front: LCS recurrence when the last characters differ?
cards.back: L(i, j) = max(L(i-1, j), L(i, j-1)).

cards.front: Why does greedy fail on 0/1 knapsack?
cards.back: Value-per-weight greedy is only optimal for fractional knapsack; small counterexamples break it.

questions.prompt: Which greedy rule is optimal for unweighted interval scheduling?
questions.explanation: Earliest finish time stays ahead of any optimal solution.

questions.prompt: What does T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) solve to?
questions.explanation: Each of the log n levels of the recursion tree does O(n) work.

questions.prompt: Why is naive recursion on the weighted interval scheduling recurrence slow?
questions.answer_text: The same subproblems are recomputed many times, so the recursion tree grows exponentially.
questions.explanation: Memoization fixes this by storing each OPT(j) once.

questions.prompt: Is the O(nW) knapsack algorithm polynomial in the input size?
questions.explanation: W takes only log W bits to write down.
